key_insight: A quantized vortex ring in pipe flow develops an energy spectrum that depends strongly on background flow velocity, enabling negative and very large effective masses and suggesting a new route to turbulence onset.
engineering_relevance: The model offers a theoretical way to estimate a critical Reynolds-like threshold for quantum turbulence and to anticipate vortex states that may destabilize flow.
method: Quantize a classical closed vortex filament using the author's earlier technique.
Analyze the vortex-ring energy spectrum E(p) as a function of total momentum p and background flow velocity v.
Compare a quantum Reynolds analogue against a critical single-vortex value to identify coupled-vortex states.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical spectrum analysis showing velocity-dependent states with negative and arbitrarily large effective masses, plus coupled vortex pairs with finite total mass.
watch_item: The conclusions are model-based and depend on an idealized infinite cylindrical pipe and a specific quantization framework, so physical validation in real flows may be nontrivial.
paper_title: Quantum vortex in a fluid flow: negative effective mass and a novel mechanism for turbulence formation
